front_blocks.md: What does satellite communication use to carry signals?

front_blocks.md: Give one advantage and two disadvantages of satellite communication.

back_blocks.md: The service is **always available**, but it can be **interrupted by weather conditions** and its signals **do not pass through solid objects**.

front_blocks.md: How does a television picture reach a home by satellite?

back_blocks.md: A video signal is **sent from a broadcaster to a satellite**, then back to earth to an **antenna connected to a set-top box** or directly to a television, which **decodes the signal**.

front_blocks.md: What is Ethernet, and what is USB used for?

back_blocks.md: **Ethernet** is the networking standard for connecting devices to a **local area network (LAN)**, while **USB** connects and powers various devices such as printers, flash drives, keyboards and mice.

front_blocks.md: Give two advantages of using a wired method to connect to a smartphone.

back_blocks.md: A wired connection is **faster, with higher bandwidth and lower latency**, gives a **more stable connection**, suffers **less interference**, is **more secure**, and needs **no password**.

front_blocks.md: Give two advantages of using a wireless method to connect to a smartphone.

back_blocks.md: The user **can move around while transferring data**, does not have to **waste time finding and connecting cables**, avoids the **cost of cables**, and there are **no trailing wires** to create a hazard.

front_blocks.md: Name five wireless methods of communication.

back_blocks.md: **Wi-Fi** connects devices to a LAN, **Bluetooth** connects two devices over very short distances, **infra-red (IR)** transmits tiny amounts of data over very short distances, **NFC** uses close proximity RFID, and **4G and 5G** provide internet access to mobile devices.

front_blocks.md: Define **local area network (LAN)**.

back_blocks.md: A local area network is a network covering a **small geographical area** (under 1 mile), where **all of the hardware is owned by the company, organisation or household using it**.

cards.front_md: Define **local area network (LAN)**.

front_blocks.md: Name three types of connection a LAN uses.

back_blocks.md: A LAN uses **unshielded twisted pair (UTP) cable**, **fibre optic cable** or **wireless connections (Wi-Fi)**.

cards.front_md: Name three types of connection a LAN uses.
cards.back_md: A LAN uses **unshielded twisted pair (UTP) cable**, **fibre optic cable** or **wireless connections (Wi-Fi)**.

front_blocks.md: Give three advantages of a LAN.

back_blocks.md: A LAN allows **centralised management** of updates, backups and software installations, lets devices be **secured** with firewalls and antivirus software, lets users **share resources** such as printers, and lets users **collaborate and share files and folders**.

cards.front_md: Give three advantages of a LAN.

front_blocks.md: Give three disadvantages of a LAN.

back_blocks.md: If **hardware fails** the network may not function, networks are **more prone to attacks** than standalone computers, access can be **slow depending on network traffic**, and they **require maintenance** which can be costly.

cards.front_md: Give three disadvantages of a LAN.

front_blocks.md: Define **wide area network (WAN)**.

back_blocks.md: A wide area network is a network covering a **large geographical area** (over 1 mile), made up of a **collection of LANs joined together**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
All the hardware used to connect a WAN is owned by the organisation using it.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

On a WAN the connecting hardware is **not all owned** by the organisation using it — telephone lines, for example, are owned by telecommunication companies. On a **LAN**, all the hardware is owned by the user.

front_blocks.md: What does a device communicate with when using Wi-Fi?

back_blocks.md: Devices communicate with a **hotspot** or a **wireless access point (WAP)**, which can be a standalone device or built into a router or switch.

front_blocks.md: Give three situations where Wi-Fi is preferred over Bluetooth.

back_blocks.md: Wi-Fi is preferred when **high speed data transfer** is required, when **long range communication** is required, and when **many devices need to be connected at the same time**.

front_blocks.md: Give three advantages of Wi-Fi.

back_blocks.md: Wi-Fi offers **portability**, since location is only limited by range, low **cost** to set up and add devices, and good **compatibility**, since most devices have a built-in Wi-Fi adapter.

front_blocks.md: What is Bluetooth typically used for?

back_blocks.md: Bluetooth is typically used for a **direct connection between two devices**, such as headphones, controllers, keyboards and mice.

front_blocks.md: What happens when two devices pair over Bluetooth?

back_blocks.md: They **exchange a cryptographic key**, which is used to generate a **secret shared key** that **encrypts the data** between them, creating a **Wireless Personal Area Network (WPAN)**.

cards.front_md: What happens when two devices pair over Bluetooth?

front_blocks.md: Give two advantages and two disadvantages of Bluetooth.

back_blocks.md: Bluetooth is **ideal for personal devices and ad-hoc connections** and has **very low power consumption**, but it has **very slow transfer speeds**, data **can be intercepted by anyone in range**, and it has a **short range**.

front_blocks.md: Define **GPS**.

back_blocks.md: Global Positioning System is a **satellite system used to track the exact location of an object**, using orbiting satellites to receive, amplify and transmit signals.

cards.front_md: Define **GPS**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
GPS works reliably without a direct line of sight.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
GPS **requires a direct line of sight**, and its signal can suffer **interference due to weather or obstacles**.

cards.front_md:

front_blocks.md: Give two advantages and two disadvantages of GPS.

back_blocks.md: GPS offers a **wide coverage area**, **real-time data transmission**, improved communication in **remote locations** and **accurate location tracking**, but it has **expensive setup and maintenance**, **signal interference**, **limited bandwidth** and raises **privacy concerns**.

front_blocks.md: What do 3G and 4G refer to, and how do they differ?

back_blocks.md: They are the **3rd and 4th generations of mobile data networks**, giving mobile devices wireless access to the internet; each generation has a **faster transfer rate** and **improved capacity for more users**.

front_blocks.md: What is infra-red used for?

back_blocks.md: Infra-red transfers **very small amounts of data** to a device in **direct line of sight**, and is commonly used in remotes to control televisions, audio receivers and home entertainment equipment.

back_blocks.md: Infra-red uses **light waves**, so **walls or obstacles can block the signal** and **sunlight can affect it**.

front_blocks.md: What is the difference between passive and active NFC?

back_blocks.md: **Passive** NFC uses **energy from the reader**, while **active** NFC **has its own power source** — smartphones use active NFC for contactless payments.
